name: Battle of Sagrajas
note: The accounts name the commanders of each division but give no compass directions and no exact lines, so the two armies are drawn facing each other across the river with the divisions in the order the accounts list them. Which side of the Christian army each division stood on, where the Christian camp lay and the nearby hill are placed on their side of the field; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. The accounts also describe the Muslim vanguard both as ten thousand Almoravid cavalry assisting Al-Mu'tamid and as a separate Almoravid force under Dawud ibn Aisha; it is drawn as one block. European accounts call the first phase of the fighting the Battle of Rueda and the second the Battle of Sacralias.

phases.title: The armies face each other across the river
phases.text: The two armies had camped facing each other with only the Wadi Bira between them. The Muslims put heavy cavalry in front and kept the Almoravid reserve hidden behind a high mound; Alfonso drew up two divisions and a vanguard.
phases.quote: The Islamic and Castilian armies set up camp facing each other, separated only by the river Wadi Bira

phases.title: The Castilian first division is thrown back
phases.text: Alfonso sent his first division against Al-Mu'tamid, but it met the Almoravid cavalry before reaching him. The Almoravid archers helped drive it back to its second line, though the Almoravids lost men.
phases.quote: Nevertheless, his reliance on a large contingent of archers played a crucial role in repelling the initial Castilian attack, compelling them to retreat to their second line of defense.

phases.title: The Andalusian front line gives ground
phases.text: The Castilian assault and its better weapons forced Al-Mu'tamid's front line back. Some Andalusian leaders fled to Badajoz, but Al-Mu'tamid and the knights of Seville held their ground, though surrounded.
phases.quote: Some Andalusian leaders fled to the city of Badajoz upon recognizing their imminent defeat. However, Al-Mu'tamid and the knights of Seville managed to maintain their positions despite being encircled by thousands of Castilian troops.

phases.title: Alfonso attacks the Almoravids with Al-Mu'tamid
phases.text: Alfonso then turned on the Almoravid horsemen supporting Al-Mu'tamid, the contingent of Dawud ibn Aisha. The pressure on Dawud and his knights grew.
phases.quote: Alfonso decided to attack the Almoravid forces supporting Al-Mu'tamid, specifically targeting the contingent led by Dawud ibn Aisha.

phases.title: Sir's battalion breaks into the Castilian army
phases.text: Dawud ibn Aisha sent word to Yusuf ibn Tashfin, who dispatched a battalion under Sir ibn Abi Bakr. It broke into the heart of the Castilian army and linked up with Al-Mu'tamid's forces.
phases.quote: This battalion successfully penetrated the heart of the Castilian army, linking up with Al-Mu'tamid's forces

phases.title: Alfonso reaches the tents and the vanguard gives way
phases.text: Alfonso kept up the pressure until he reached the Almoravid tents and breached the trench round them. Al-Mu'tamid's Andalusian forces were driven back, and the Castilians went after them.
phases.quote: advancing until he reached the tents of the Almoravids and breached the trench protecting them

phases.title: The reserve strikes the Castilian camp
phases.text: While the Castilians chased Al-Mu'tamid, Yusuf ibn Tashfin brought up his reserve and attacked their camp. The Castilian horses panicked at the camels, which he set ablaze, and the camp's remaining men fled towards Alfonso.
phases.quote: He advanced with his reserve forces and attacked the Castilian camp

phases.title: Alfonso halts his pursuit and falls back
phases.text: Alfonso learned of the chaos in his camp and gave up the chase of Al-Mu'tamid, withdrawing to save his stronghold.
phases.quote: Alfonso halted his pursuit of Al-Mu'tamid and retreated to save his stronghold from disaster

phases.title: Al-Mu'tamid orders an attack and Sir charges
phases.text: Al-Mu'tamid ordered his companions to attack as Alfonso fell back, and Sir ibn Abi Bakr and his men charged. The soldiers who had fled to Badajoz came back into the fight.
phases.quote: Commander Sir ibn Abi Bakr and his men charged at Alfonso's forces, increasing the pressure and continuing the rout.

phases.title: The Takrur cavalry charge
phases.text: Yusuf ibn Tashfin ordered 4,000 black cavalry from Takrur to charge. Their charge destroyed the Christian cavalry.
phases.quote: The turning point occurred when Ibn Tashfin ordered 4,000 black cavalry from Takrur to charge into the fray.

phases.title: Alfonso retreats to a hill and escapes at night
phases.text: As the sun began to set, Alfonso retreated with a small contingent to a nearby hill and later escaped in the dark.
phases.quote: As the sun began to set and realizing defeat was imminent, Alfonso retreated with a small contingent to a nearby hill
